subject: GNG mean vs median model parameters

messages.author: e8e2387233c35cd4
messages.subject: GNG mean vs median model parameters
parts:
Dear all,
we are currently doing some reanalysis for data we have analysed some time ago. 
We used gng_m4 for patient data, at the time we modelled means and medians for individual subject parameters. Now, doing a clustering analysis we find that the median parameters classify groups nearly perfectly, while the means provide a poor fit. 

If I understand that correctly, the mean and the median simply describes how the parameter is summarised by subject.

If we are thinking of learning rate for example then is it correct to assume that for the mean  this means that from trial to trial the learning rate is being updated based on the mean distribution of the past trials, where as for the median it would be the median distribution? Therefore using the median would (as it always does) take extreme behaviour less into account?

Thank you very much for your help.
Franziska

messages.author: 47d1400f432367d7
messages.subject: Re: GNG mean vs median model parameters
parts:
Hi Franziska,

The mean/median is computed as the mean or median of the posterior distributions for each person. So, it is really just a way to summarize the parameter estimates for each person. In other words, the posterior distribution itself is unchanged whether you use the mean/median argument when fitting (Stan is estimating the full posterior distribution). You could actually compute the posterior means/medians with the fitted model parameters if interested, we only include the argument for convenience. 

Let me know if that is clear!

Best,
Nate

messages.subject: Re: GNG mean vs median model parameters
parts:
Hello, 

I think the description about learning rate example is not right.
The way how to summarize posterior distribution to point estimate (i,e, mean median mode) has pros and cons 
Please see https://mmeredith.net/blog/2019/Mean_median_mode.htm
I think you need to look for entire shape of the posterior distribution to justify using the median value.
I also think it is better to rather emphasize on group parameters than individual parameters, since hBayesDM uses hierarchical model 

Best wishes, 
Minchul

Hello Minchul,
Thanks for the comment, and pointing me to the median/mode/mean differentiation. It did make it a lot clearer.

I am not sure about your last comment - hBayesDM estimates individual and group parameters simultaneously, so individual parameters should be more stable as they account for the behaviour of the entire group, so it should be appropriate to use individual parameters?!

This leads me to two questions/scenarios for which I would very much appreciate your comment:
1) When dealing with various predefined groups, would you recommend modelling them separately, to account for group inherent traits? Meaning comparison of group parameters would be appropriate. If I model groups separately, would I not bias the data, especially when the data sets are small (e.g. n=30)? 

2) However when dealing with exactly the same dataset, and wanting to applying data driven clustering to investigate whether subject groups can be classified using individual group-informed parameters, then those parameters would need to be generated from one model containing no information about group (modelling all participants together)?    

Thank you. Best. Franziska

messages.author: 78b6642bb15bbd88
messages.subject: Re: GNG mean vs median model parameters
parts:
Hello, Franziska

I am not a statistic person, and my comments can be wrong - I wonder what the hBayesDM developers think.
I mentioned about the group parameters because of the 'Shrinkage' in hierarchical models.
I cannot mathematically prove, but due to shrinkage one's individual parameter estimates would regress toward group mean,
rather than reflecting one's characteristic.
But hierarchical model pools  individual data so this effect makes the group parameter reliable, even though small number of subjects 
(I think 30 people is enough to estimate group paratmeter)

For the questions, I think what is important is your theory about the data.
If you think the participants data are drawn from different group parameters, I think you should fit model separately for each groups, vice versa.
OR I think you can fit both hypothesis (one group or two groups) and to Bayesian model comparison to choose winning model.

Best wishes, 
Minchul

messages.author: 4bcf82a01cf98f56
messages.subject: Re: GNG mean vs median model parameters
parts:
Hi Franziska,

In a hierarchical Bayesian framework, group and individual parameters are estimated simultaneously. For each individual, there's an individual posterior distribution and we can calculate its summary statistics like posterior mean (the mean of a posterior distribution) or posterior median. By default, hBayesDM calculates the means of individual posterior distributions and contain them in 'indPars'. 

Hope this helps.

Best,
Young

we are currently doing some reanalysis for data we have analysed some time ago. 
We used gng_m4 for patient data, at the time we modelled means and medians for individual subject parameters. Now, doing a clustering analysis we find that the median parameters classify groups nearly perfectly, while the means provide a poor fit. 

If I understand that correctly, the mean and the median simply describes how the parameter is summarised by subject.

If we are thinking of learning rate for example then is it correct to assume that for the mean  this means that from trial to trial the learning rate is being updated based on the mean distribution of the past trials, where as for the median it would be the median distribution? Therefore using the median would (as it always does) take extreme behaviour less into account?

Thank you very much for your help.
Franziska

parts:
Dear Young, 
thanks for explaining!

I am trying to generate integrated loglikelihoods per subject to describe model fit per subject using the gng_m4. Is there a way to integrate/extract that automatically from the model?

Thank you.
Franziska
On 30. Sep 2021, at 18:57, wooyou...@gmail.com <wooyou...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hi Franziska,

In a hierarchical Bayesian framework, group and individual parameters are estimated simultaneously. For each individual, there's an individual posterior distribution and we can calculate its summary statistics like posterior mean (the mean of a posterior distribution) or posterior median. By default, hBayesDM calculates the means of individual posterior distributions and contain them in 'indPars'. 

Hope this helps.

Best,
Young


On Thursday, September 30, 2021 at 3:02:17 AM UTC+9 franzis...@gmail.com wrote:
Thanks Minchul, those are helpful comments - and this is also indeed the strategy I would have followed. Thanks. BW.

On 29. Sep 2021, at 09:45, MCkim <minch...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hello, Franziska

I am not a statistic person, and my comments can be wrong - I wonder what the hBayesDM developers think.
I mentioned about the group parameters because of the 'Shrinkage' in hierarchical models.
I cannot mathematically prove, but due to shrinkage one's individual parameter estimates would regress toward group mean,
rather than reflecting one's characteristic.
But hierarchical model pools  individual data so this effect makes the group parameter reliable, even though small number of subjects 
(I think 30 people is enough to estimate group paratmeter)

For the questions, I think what is important is your theory about the data.
If you think the participants data are drawn from different group parameters, I think you should fit model separately for each groups, vice versa.
OR I think you can fit both hypothesis (one group or two groups) and to Bayesian model comparison to choose winning model.

Best wishes, 
Minchul

2021년 9월 29일 수요일 오후 4시 20분 11초 UTC+9에 franzis...@gmail.com님이 작성:
Hello Minchul,
Thanks for the comment, and pointing me to the median/mode/mean differentiation. It did make it a lot clearer.

I am not sure about your last comment - hBayesDM estimates individual and group parameters simultaneously, so individual parameters should be more stable as they account for the behaviour of the entire group, so it should be appropriate to use individual parameters?!

This leads me to two questions/scenarios for which I would very much appreciate your comment:
1) When dealing with various predefined groups, would you recommend modelling them separately, to account for group inherent traits? Meaning comparison of group parameters would be appropriate. If I model groups separately, would I not bias the data, especially when the data sets are small (e.g. n=30)? 

2) However when dealing with exactly the same dataset, and wanting to applying data driven clustering to investigate whether subject groups can be classified using individual group-informed parameters, then those parameters would need to be generated from one model containing no information about group (modelling all participants together)?    

Thank you. Best. Franziska

On 29. Sep 2021, at 07:04, MCkim <minch...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hello, 

I think the description about learning rate example is not right.
The way how to summarize posterior distribution to point estimate (i,e, mean median mode) has pros and cons 
Please see https://mmeredith.net/blog/2019/Mean_median_mode.htm
I think you need to look for entire shape of the posterior distribution to justify using the median value.
I also think it is better to rather emphasize on group parameters than individual parameters, since hBayesDM uses hierarchical model 

Best wishes, 
Minchul

2021년 9월 29일 수요일 오전 3시 35분 29초 UTC+9에 franzis...@gmail.com님이 작성:
Hi Nate,
Thanks for getting back. So just to get that right, the posterior distribution is generated for each parameter over the all trials, and then mean/median can be called using indPars which defines the individual parameter? 
Thanks & BW
Franziska

 
On 28. Sep 2021, at 16:05, Haines, Nathaniel B. <haine...@buckeyemail.osu.edu> wrote:

Hi Franziska,

The mean/median is computed as the mean or median of the posterior distributions for each person. So, it is really just a way to summarize the parameter estimates for each person. In other words, the posterior distribution itself is unchanged whether you use the mean/median argument when fitting (Stan is estimating the full posterior distribution). You could actually compute the posterior means/medians with the fitted model parameters if interested, we only include the argument for convenience. 

Let me know if that is clear!

Best,
Nate
